Patterns describe associations, not causes or diagnoses. Themes and written tone are estimates from English text. Uncertain text and missing data are left out. resources.string: A little space to make Daily Pause yours.
A quiet place to check in, reflect, and begin again.
Daily Pause is a private space to check in with your mood, reflect on what’s on your mind, and make room for yourself.
Write freely, organize journals into Heaps, and look back at your Analytics to explore your Mood Graph and private weekly patterns.

Your saved journals stay on this device unless you export or choose an encrypted backup. My Journal and Analytics are protected by your PIN or enrolled biometrics. Weather sends your chosen city or rounded coordinates to Open-Meteo; your journal text, moods, and answers are never sent with weather requests.
Choose the appearance that feels comfortable for you.
Your choice is remembered the next time you open Daily Pause.
Choose a Heap for this journal, or select No to save outside Heaps. Unlock My Journal to view your Heaps or create a new one.
Unlock to choose a Heap for your moment. Your writing is still saved as a draft.
Your Heaps couldn’t be opened. Your moment is still saved as a draft. Please try again.

Some days, just existing is a win. Take the win. Stretch for a few minutes, take a short walk, or lie down and stare at the wall for a bit. If it helps, reach out to someone you trust.\n\nFeel like leaving a few words here? Future you can look back and see what helped you get through days like this.

Hard days spare no one. If you can, take five minutes to yourself, sit in a little quiet, or chat with someone you love.\n\nA few words about today might help you unpack it. Later, you can look back and see how you made it through.
Fun fact: “OK” started as a jokey “oll korrect” (“all correct”). An imperfect little win still counts!\n\nJot down what made today feel okay. Future you might spot the little things that helped.
Glad to hear it! Keep that rhythm going.\n\nWhat helped make today a good one? Leave yourself a few notes so future you can come back to the feeling, or borrow a little inspiration on a tougher day.
Awesome. No notes. Just. Awesome.\n\nOkay, maybe a few notes! Capture what made today great so future you can relive it and remember how good a day can feel.
Use a passphrase of 12 to 256 characters.

Daily Pause is a quiet place to check in with yourself, put feelings into words, and notice what helps you feel more like you.
Let your thoughts out. Keep journals together in Heaps for the different parts of your life.
Look back with kindness. Discover mood patterns as your daily reflections grow.
Your journals stay on this device unless you choose to export or back them up. Private views are protected by your journal lock.
Start here each day. Take a breath, notice how you feel, and make a little room for yourself. Tap Next whenever you are ready.
Choose the emotion that feels closest, from Low to Great. A mood alone is enough for a check-in; there is no right or wrong answer.
Use the optional prompts to write about your day, your thoughts, and what you need. Save this moment keeps your mood and words as a journal, inside a Heap or on their own.
A little context for your day

Your daily forecast appears here with the high, low, and general conditions. Choose a city or allow approximate location in Settings → Weather. Weather available when you save a moment stays with that journal.
Come here to revisit your reflections. Keep entries on their own or organize them into Heaps by topic, concern, or facet of life. Your PIN or enrolled biometrics protects this private space.
Add a journal or a Heap
The + button offers a new journal entry or a new Heap. Give a Heap a name, with an optional category and color. Heaps help compartmentalize thoughts and clear a little more room in your mind.
Analytics opens a menu with Mood Graph and Mood Analysis. Both stay behind your journal lock. Next, take a look at what each view can show you.
Mood Graph shows how your recorded moods move over time. Choose a week, month, three months, year, or custom date range. Multiple check-ins are averaged, and missing days stay as gaps.

Mood Analysis looks for weather, journal-response, and time-related patterns on your device. It starts after at least 30 distinct days of journaling in the recent 90 days, then reassesses weekly. These are possible associations to reflect on, not causes or diagnoses. Keep checking in; your insights will grow with you. Tap Next to finish.
